name: Example: Solving Natural Logarithmic Equations by First Rearranging the Equation
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)-2 & =13 \\ 3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1) & =15 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the natural logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the natural logarithm is $e,$ so we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1) & =5 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)} & ={e}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we know that $e^{\ln (5x+1)} = 5x+1.$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+1 & ={e}^{5} \\ 5x & ={e}^{5}-1 \\ x & =\frac{{e}^{5}-1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
